appraisal_events.evidence: Swann forçait avec tant de cynisme [ses amis] à lui servir d'entremetteurs... une habileté diplomatique qui... accusait un caractère permanent et des buts identiques; mon grand-père, reconnaissant l'écriture de Swann, s'écriait : 'Voilà Swann qui va demander quelque chose : à la garde !' et mes grands-parents opposaient une fin de non-recevoir absolue aux prières les plus faciles à satisfaire qu'il leur adressait.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly frames Swann's habitual use of loyal friends and even trusted family as instrumental go-betweens for his romantic pursuits as cynical and self-interested; the grandparents' wary refusal of his simple requests confirms that even affectionate intimates have learned to guard themselves against him.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator's explicit characterization of Swann's diplomatic persistence in soliciting favors as 'cynisme,' revealing a fixed, self-serving pattern beneath his charm, clearly lowers his local standing.
The grandparents meet his easiest requests with an absolute refusal, guardedly withholding the small social favor he wants and treating his approach with suspicion rather than welcome.
